result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, sidewalks, and curb ramps within a mixed-use urban environment. However, safety is limited by the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and significant sightline obstructions caused by vehicles parked close to the crossing.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are positioned immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, blocking the visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on the right side of the main roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is signalized for vehicles but lacks visible walk/don't-walk indicators for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light poles at the intersection corners

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The roadway surface shows significant cracking and patching, which can create tripping hazards or cause vehicles to swerve.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the roadway

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and continuous sidewalks. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway lacks a pedestrian refuge island and visible pedestrian-specific signal heads, increasing exposure for those crossing.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a refuge island, increasing exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install visible pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. However, the wide crossing distance and lack of physical traffic calming or medians increase pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic in a residential setting.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the intersection increases the time pedestrians are exposed to moving traffic without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners can block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.
